trait.description: An index to express the proportion of standing leaves without the typical late-stage symptoms of black leaf streak disease, i.e. a black spot with a necrotic centre. It also corrects for the difference in the number of leaves produced by different types of bananas.

method.description: Calculate as: 100 multiplied by (Youngest leaf spotted, minus 1), divided by Number of standing leaves, e.g. 100 * (6 - 1) / 12 = 42.

method.methodName: Black leaf streak disease severity index - computation
method.description: Calculate as: ((((Number of leaves with black leaf streak disease severity grade 0, multiplied by 0), plus (Number of leaves with black leaf streak disease severity grade 1, multiplied by 1), plus (Number of leaves with black leaf streak disease severity grade 2, multiplied by 2), plus (Number of leaves with black leaf streak disease severity grade 3, multiplied by 3), plus (Number of leaves with black leaf streak disease severity grade 4, multiplied by 4), plus (Number of leaves with black leaf streak disease severity grade 5, multiplied by 5), plus (Number of leaves with black leaf streak disease severity grade 6, multiplied by 6)), divided by the number of grades in the scale minus 1 (i.e. 7-1)), divided by the Number of standing leaves), multiplied by 100. For example, ((((3 * 0) + (1 * 1) + (1 * 2) + (3 * 3) + (5 * 4) + (0 * 5) + (0 * 6)) / 6) / 13) * 100 = ((32 / 6) / 13) * 100 = 41.
method.formula: ((?nb)/(N-1)T) x 100. Where n = the number of leaves in each disease severity grade (0-6, based on Gauhls modification of Stovers severity scoring system), b = grade, N = number of grades in the scale (7), T = total number of leaves scored.

method.methodName: Root necrosis caused by nematodes - estimation
method.description: Select at random five functional primary roots, at least 10 cm long. Reduce the length of the five selected roots to 10 cm and slice through the roots length-wise. Evaluate one half of each of the five roots for the percentage of root cortex showing necrosis. The maximum root necrosis per root half can be 20 %, giving a maximum root necrosis of 100 % for the five halves together. Mentally determine the necrosis of the individual roots (1 to 5) and sum these together to get the total root necrosis of the sample.

Where root knot nematode galls are present, determine the extent of the galling using the scale.

method.description: Collect all roots from a standard size excavation of 20 x 20 x 20 cm extending outwards from the corm of the plant. Take only roots from the selected plant. Carefully wash the soil from the roots with tap water. Cut the roots into 1 cm pieces. Take a subsample of 5 g, add 100 ml distilled water and store the roots at 4 degrees Celsius. Stain the egg masses by immersing the roots in 0.15 g/L phloxine B for 15 mins. Count the number of egg-laying females under a stereo microscope.

method.description: Calculate as: the time elapsed between the Date of harvest of the bunch of the plant from the preceeding crop cycle and the Date of death of the current plant, e.g. 24/03/2015 - 24/12/2014 = 90 days.

trait.description: The time elapsed from the harvest of the bunch of the plant from the preceding crop cycle to the harvest of the bunch of the plant from the current crop cycle.

method.description: Calculate as: the time elapsed between the Date of harvest of the bunch of the plant from the preceeding crop cycle and the Date of harvest of the bunch of the plant from the current crop cycle, e.g. 24/11/2015 - 24/12/2014 = 335 days.

trait.traitName: Plant height to neck of peduncle
trait.description: The height of the pseudostem of the plant from the collar to the curved neck of the peduncle.

method.methodName: Plant height - neck of peduncle - measurement
method.description: Measure the distance from the collar, or from the pseudostem base at the ground if the collar is not visible, to under the neck of the curved peduncle, using a measuring pole or sliding ruler.

trait.description: The number of water suckers (suckers with broad leaves, a small rhizome, and a weak connection to the plant) in the mat.

method.description: Estimate maturity stage of the bunch.

trait.description: The weight of the rachis.

method.description: Cut the hands off the rachis and weigh the rachis, using scales.

trait.description: The weight of all the hands of the bunch, excluding the rachis.

method.description: Calculate as: the Bunch weight, minus the Rachis weight, e.g. 50 - 10 = 40.

trait.description: The rank (order) of a hand in the bunch.

method.description: Record the rank (order) of the second-most distal hand in the bunch, starting with the hand at the proximal end (closest to the pseudostem) of the bunch as 1 and continuing to the hand at the most distal end (closest to the male bud).

trait.traitName: Multiple number of fingers in hand
trait.description: The number of fingers in multiple hands.

method.methodName: Multiple number of fingers in hand - counting
method.description: Count how many fingers are in multiple hands. Associate the data with the Hand rank and the Number of hands measured. The recommendation is to collect this data from the second and second-most distal hands.

trait.description: The number of hands used to obtain a measurement.
trait.attribute: Number used to obtain a measurement

method.description: Count how many hands are used to obtain a measurement.

trait.traitName: Average number of fingers in hand
trait.description: The average number of fingers in a hand.

method.methodName: Average number of fingers in hand - hands - computation
method.description: Calculate as: the sum of the Number of fingers in hand, divided by the Number of hands in bunch, e.g. (10 + 10 + 11 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 12 + 12 + 12 + 11 +12 + 12 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 11) / 16 = 10.8.

trait.traitName: Calculated number of fingers in bunch
trait.description: The estimated number of fingers in the bunch based on a calculation using the number of fingers in the third and second-most distal hands and the number of hands in the bunch.

method.methodName: Number of fingers in bunch - estimation
method.description: Calculate as: the sum of the Number of fingers in 3rd hand and the Number of fingers in 2nd-most distal hand, divided by 2, and multiplied by the Number of hands in bunch, e.g. (16 + 12) / 2 * 8 = 112.

trait.description: The weight of multiple hands.

method.description: Cut multiple hands from the rachis and weigh them together, using scales. Associate the data with the Hank rank and the Number of hands measured.

trait.description: The average weight of the hands.

method.description: Calculate as: the Total finger weight, divided by the Number of hands in bunch, e.g. 46.8 / 16 = 2.9.

trait.description: The weight of multiple fingers.

method.description: Weigh multiple fingers together, using scales. Associate the data with the Hank rank and the Number of fingers measured. The recommendation is to collect this data from six fingers in total - three fingers in the middle of the outer whorl from the second hand and from the second-most distal hand.

trait.description: The number of fingers used to obtain a measurement.
trait.attribute: Number used to obtain a measurement

method.description: Count how many fingers are used to obtain a measurement.

trait.description: The average weight of the fingers.

method.description: Calculate as: the sum of the the Finger weight measurements, divided by the number of those measurements, e.g. (150 + 146 + 147 + 152 + 140 + 146) / 6 = 147.

trait.description: The average length of the fingers measured along the external (dorsal) arc, excluding the pedicel and the fruit tip.

method.description: Calculate as: the sum of the Finger external length measurements, divided by the number of those measurements, e.g. (30 + 34 + 32 + 33 + 33 + 31) / 6 = 32.1.

trait.description: The length of a finger measured along the internal (ventral) arc, excluding the pedicel and the fruit tip.

method.description: Measure the length of a finger, along the internal (ventral) arc, excluding the pedicel and the fruit tip, using a tape measure. Associate the data with the Hand rank and the Number of fingers measured. The recommendation is to collect this data from six fingers in total - three fingers in the middle of the outer whorl from the second hand and from the second-most distal hand.

trait.description: The average length of the fingers measured along the internal (ventral) arc, excluding the pedicel and the fruit tip.

method.description: Calculate as: the sum of the Finger internal length measurements, divided by the number of those measurements, e.g. (27 + 31 + 29 + 30 + 30 + 28) / 6 = 29.2.

trait.description: The circumference of a finger.

method.description: Measure the circumference of a finger at its widest point, using a tape measure. Associate the data with the Hand rank. The recommendation is to collect this data from six fingers in total - three fingers in the middle of the outer whorl from the second hand and from the second-most distal hand.

trait.description: The average circumference of the fingers.

method.description: Calculate as: the sum of the Finger circumference measurements, divided by the number of those measurements, e.g. (7.0 + 8.0 + 9.0 + 10.0 + 7.0 + 9.5) / 6 = 8.4.

trait.description: The lateral (side to side) diameter of a finger.

method.description: Measure the lateral diameter of a finger from the left to the right side (not from the ventral to the dorsal side), at the widest point, using calipers. Associate the data with the Hand rank. The recommendation is to collect this data from six fingers in total - three fingers in the middle of the outer whorl from the second hand and from the second-most distal hand.

trait.description: The average lateral (side to side) diameter of a finger.

method.description: Calculate as: the sum of the Finger lateral diameter measurements, divided by the number of those measurements, e.g. (3.5 + 5.2 + 4.1 + 5 + 6 + 6.8) / 6 = 5.1.

trait.description: The lateral (side to side) diameter of the pulp of a fruit.

method.description: Cut a finger in half, crosswise at its widest point, and on the cross-section measure the lateral diameter of the fruit pulp, from the left to the right side (not from the ventral to the dorsal side), using calipers. Associate the data with the Hand rank. The recommendation is to collect this data from six fingers in total - three fingers in the middle of the outer whorl from the second hand and from the second-most distal hand.

trait.description: The average lateral (side to side) diameter of the pulp of a fruit.
trait.attribute: Average lateral diameter of the pulp

method.methodName: Average fruit pulp lateral diameter - computation
method.description: Calculate as: the sum of the Fruit pulp lateral diameter measurements, divided by the number of those measurements, e.g. (3.1 + 4.8 + 3.7 + 4.6 + 5.6 + 6.4) / 6 = 4.7.

trait.description: The average thickness of the peel of a finger.

method.description: Calculate as: the sum of the Finger peel thickness measurements, divided by the number of those measurements, e.g. (2 + 2 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 3) / 6 = 2.

trait.description: The number of plants that are planted.

method.description: Calculate as: the sum of the number of values for Date of planting.

trait.description: The area allocated to one plant.

method.description: Calculate as: multiply the distance of the spacing between the plants, both latitudinally and longitudinally, e.g. 2 m x 3 m = 6 m2.

trait.description: The number of plants that are planted, in a defined area.

method.description: Calculate as: number of square metres in the area unit of choice, divided by the Plant spacing, e.g. 10,000 square metres in 1 hectare / 6 = 1,667 plants/ha.

trait.description: The number of plants that are dead.
trait.attribute: Combined number of plants that are dead

method.description: Calculate as: the sum of the number of values for Date of death.

trait.description: The number of plants that are harvested.

method.description: Calculate as: the sum of the number of values for Date of harvest.

trait.description: The number of plants that are alive but not harvested (e.g. due to slow or poor development).
trait.attribute: Combined number of plants not harvested

method.methodName: Number of plants not harvested - computation
method.description: Calculate as: the Number of plants planted, minus the Number of plants dead, minus the Number of plants harvested, e.g. 24 - 4 - 18 = 2.

trait.description: The proportion of plants that are dead, from the number of plants planted.
trait.attribute: Combined proportion of plants that are dead

method.description: Calculate as: the Number of plants dead, divided by the Number of plants planted, e.g. 4 / 24 = 0.17.

trait.description: The number of plants that are dead, in a defined area.
trait.attribute: Combined density of plants that are dead

method.description: Calculate as: the Plant density multiplied by the Death proportion, e.g. 1,667 * 0.17 = 283.

trait.description: The proportion of plants that are harvested, from the number of plants planted.

method.description: Calculate as: the Number of plants harvested, divided by the Number of plants planted, e.g. 18 / 24 = 0.75.

trait.description: The number of plants that are harvested, in a defined area.

method.description: Calculate as: the Plant density multiplied by the Harvest proportion, e.g. 1,667 * 0.75 = 1,250.

trait.description: The proportion of plants that are alive but not harvested (e.g. due to slow or poor development), from the number of plants planted.
trait.attribute: Combined proportion of plants not harvested

method.description: Calculate as: the Number of plants not harvested, divided by the Number of plants planted, e.g. 2 / 24 = 0.08.

trait.description: The number of plants that are alive but not harvested (e.g. due to slow or poor development), in a defined area.
trait.attribute: Combined density of plants not harvested

method.description: Calculate as: the Plant density multiplied by the Non-harvest proportion, e.g. 1,667 * 0.08 = 133.

trait.description: The proportion of the crop cycle that takes place in one year.
trait.attribute: Proportion of crop cycle that takes place in one year

method.description: Calculate as: the length of a year (e.g. 365 days) divided by the Plant crop cycle or the Ratoon crop cycle, e.g. 365 / 334 = 1.09.

trait.description: The bunch weight produced by the plant over the course of the crop cycle, averaged across one year.

method.description: Calculate as: the Bunch weight multiplied by the Annual crop cycle proportion, e.g. 48 * 1.09 = 52.32.

trait.description: The average actual annual yield, taking into account the proportion of plants harvested, from the number of plants planted

method.description: Calculate as: the Bunch weight divided by 1,000, multiplied by the Annual crop cycle proportion, multiplied by the Harvest density, e.g. (50 / 1,000) * 1.09 * 1,250 = 68.13.

trait.description: The average potential annual yield, assuming that all plants are harvested, from the number of plants planted.

method.description: Calculate as: the Bunch weight divided by 1,000, multiplied by the Annual crop cycle proportion, multiplied by the Plant density, e.g. (50 / 1,000) * 1.09 * 1,667 = 90.85.

method.description: Collect all roots from a standard-size excavation of 20 x 20 x 20 cm extending outwards from the corm of the plant. Take only roots from the selected plant, do not include roots from adjacent plants. Carefully wash the soil from the roots with tap water. Cut the roots into 10 cm long pieces and dry with paper tissue. Take a subsample of 15 g, add 100 ml distilled water and store the roots at 4 degrees Celsius. Put the roots in 100 ml of distilled water in a kitchen blender. Macerate the roots 3 times for 10 secs (separated by 5 sec intervals). Pour the macerated suspension through 250, 106 and 40 micro-metre sieves and rinse the sieves with tap water. Using distilled water, collect in a beaker the nematodes from the 40 micro-metre sieve. Using distilled water, dilute to 200 ml the nematode suspension in a graduated cylinder. Blow air through the nematode suspension with a pipette (to homogenise the suspension). Take a subsample of 6 ml (counting dish) or 2 ml (counting slide). Count the nematodes in the counting dish (stereo microscope) or in the counting slide (light microscope). Calculate the final nematode population per unit of fresh root weight.

scale.scaleName: Faures stages of development of BLS disease scale (1987)

categories: 1 = Stage 1 appears as a small depigmentation spot whose whitish or yellow colour resembles stage 1 of Yellow Sigatoka disease. These symptoms are not visible in transmitted light and can be observed only on the underside of the leaf.

2 = Stage 2 appears as a stripe, generally brown in colour and visible on the underside of the leaf, later the symptom also appears on the upper part of the limb as a stripe, the yellow colour of which resembles the stripe at stage 1 of Yellow Sigatoka. The colour of this stripe will change progressively from brown and later to black on the upper side of the limb, but will retain the brown colour on the underside.
3 = Stage 3 differs from the previous one by its dimensions. The stripe becomes longer, is enlarged and in certain conditions (weak inoculum and unfavourable climatic conditions) can reach 2 or 3 cm.
4 = Stage 4 appears on the underside as a brown spot and on the upper side as a black spot.
5 = Stage 5 is when the elliptical spot is totally black and has spread to the underside of the limb. It is surrounded by a yellow halo with the centre beginning to flatten out.

6 = Stage 6 is when the centre of the spot dries out, turns clear gray and is surrounded by a well-defined black ring, which is, in turn, surrounded by a bright yellow halo. These spots remain visible after the leaf has dried out because the ring persists.

categories: 1 = Initial speck stage: symptoms are first visible to the naked eye as faint, minute (less than 0.25 mm diam), reddish brown specks on the lower surface of the leaf. Specks are often most abundant near the margin of the left side of the leaf, particularly towards the tip. Where leaf spot is severe, specks have been observed on the second leaf of plants that have not yet produced a bunch. Elsewhere they usually appear on the third, fourth, or older leaves.

2 = First streak stage: the initial speck elongates, becoming slightly wider, to form a characteristic narrow, reddish brown streak up to 20 mm long and 2.0 mm wide, with the long axis parallel to the leaf venation. At this stage, streaks are more clearly visible on the lower surface of the leaf than on the upper one. The distribution of streaks is variable. Sometimes they are most numerous near the edge of the left side of the leaf. At other times they are equally numerous on both sides of the leaf, and more or less evenly distributed. Frequently they are densely aggregated in a band several cm wide on one side or both sides of the mid-rib, becoming less numerous towards the edge of the leaf. Streaks may be so numerous that every cm2 of leaf surface bears one or more. There is considerable variation in the length of individual streaks on a given leaf, and they frequently overlap to form larger, compound streaks.

3 = Second-streak stage: the streaks may elongate slightly, but the most notable change is that in colour from reddish brown to dark brown or almost black, sometimes with a purplish tinge. The streak is now clearly visible on the upper surface of the leaf. The distribution of streaks at this stage of development varies in the same way as mentioned above. When streaks are very numerous, and more or less evenly distributed, the entire leaf blackens.

4 = First-spot stage: the streak broadens and becomes more or less fusiform and elliptical in outline and similar to the first-spot stage of Sigatoka (Leach 1946). The transition from streak to spot is further characterised by the development of a light brown, water-soaked border around the spot. This water-soaked effect is especially clear in the early morning, when dew is still present on the leaf, or after rain.

5 = Second-spot stage: the dark brown or black central area of the spot becomes slightly depressed and the water-soaked border becomes more pronounced due to darkening. At this stage, a slight yellowing of the leaf tissue immediately surrounding the water-soaked border may occur.

6 = Third or mature spot stage: the centre of the spot dries out, becoming light grey or buff-coloured, and further depressed. The spot is surrounded by a narrow, well-defined, dark brown or black border. between the latter and the normal green colour of the leaf, there is often a bright yellow transitional zone. After the leaf has collapsed and withered, spots remain clearly visible because of the light-coloured centre and dark border.

method.methodName: Nematode root knot galling presence - estimation
method.description: Collect all roots from a standard-size excavation of 20 x 20 x 20 cm extending outwards from the corm of the plant. Take only roots from the selected plant. Divide the collected roots into two categories: dead roots, functional roots. Dead roots are completely rotten or shrivelled whereas functional roots show at least some healthy tissue. From the functional roots, randomly select five primary roots that are at least 10 cm, and reduce their length to 10 cm. Determine the presence/absence of root knot nematodes, observed externally as galls on the roots.
